subject.title: [Feature]: Feishu Group Chat SubAgents for User-Specific Skills and Memory

question: Should OpenClaw support automatic per-user Feishu group-chat agents with isolated skill/config/memory state, and if so should that live as Feishu-plugin behavior, a generic channel SDK seam, or a core orchestration feature?
rationale: The remaining work is not a narrow bug fix: it chooses dynamic agent lifecycle, persisted config writes, skill authority, memory isolation, message delivery, and security semantics for multi-user group chats.

options.title: Feishu plugin design first
options.body: Prototype and review the group sender lifecycle in the Feishu plugin using current session, binding, and subagent hooks, then promote only proven missing seams to the SDK.

options.title: Generic channel SDK contract
options.body: Design a cross-channel per-sender agent/profile contract before extending Feishu so Telegram, Discord, Slack, and other channels do not diverge.

options.title: Decline automatic group agents
options.body: Keep current per-sender group sessions and manual configured agents, and avoid adding a heavy dynamic group-agent hierarchy.

recommendation.title: Feishu plugin design first
recommendation.body: Prototype and review the group sender lifecycle in the Feishu plugin using current session, binding, and subagent hooks, then promote only proven missing seams to the SDK.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available routing candidate from recent Feishu/session review context and adjacent current-main work.
